faqs.q: What happens during a behavioural consultation?
faqs.a: Gaynor will first talk with you about the problems you're having with your dog and what has led up to this point, so she can gather the information she needs to diagnose the problem. She'll then test your dog's behaviour — using A1K9 dogs as stooge dogs if necessary — before explaining what she believes the problem is and its most probable cause, and showing you the techniques and equipment needed to rehabilitate your dog.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral from my vet?
faqs.a: With a referral from your vet you can book a consultation with Gaynor, and you may be able to use your pet insurance to pay for it. Gaynor is a canine behaviour practitioner with the Canine and Feline Behaviour Association, which is approved by most pet insurance companies.

faqs.q: Can you help if my dog is aggressive to other dogs?
faqs.a: Yes. Dog on dog aggression consultations are highly skilled work Gaynor has a great deal of experience in — she has worked with dogs that exhibit this behaviour for 15 years, attending courses with the Canine and Feline Behaviour Association and Middlesex University to expand her knowledge, and works with all breeds of dogs no matter how serious the problem.

faqs.q: Can you help if my dog is aggressive to people?
faqs.a: Yes. Dog on person aggression consultations are highly skilled work Gaynor has a great deal of experience in — she has worked with dogs that exhibit this behaviour for 15 years, attending courses with the Canine and Feline Behaviour Association and Middlesex University to expand her knowledge, and has worked with all breeds of dogs no matter how serious the problem.

Gaynor may ask you to attend a behavioural modification programme, or to stay in touch by email or telephone so she can monitor your progress. After the consultation she writes a full report and sends a copy to your vet, unless you request otherwise.
Consultations can be held at A1K9 Behaviour and Training Academy or at your home.
